chunks: And from him, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): We were tested and were on a ship, and we spent the night and could not find a place to exit. He said: 'The companions of the ship do not pray our day as long as we hope to exit.' Then he said: 'Indeed my father used to say: That is the prayer of Noah (peace be upon him). Do you not accept that you pray the prayer of Noah?' I said: Yes, may I be your ransom. He said: 'Do not be distressed, for Noah had prayed on the ship.' I said: Standing or sitting? He said: 'Rather, standing.' I said: For I sometimes face the Qibla and the ship turns. He said: 'Determine the Qibla to the best of your ability.'

key_terms.صَلَاةُ نُوحٍ: The prayer of Noah (peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for prayer on a moving ship when the Qibla direction changes?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the specific fiqh of *Salat al-Safar* (traveler's prayer) aboard a vessel, emphasizing that the standing posture (*qayim*) is preferred over sitting unless incapacitated. It highlights the principle of *ijtihad* in determining the Qibla during movement, instructing the traveler to face the direction of the Kaaba to the best of their ability (*bi-jahdika*) without excessive worry (*la yadīqanna ṣadraka*). This ruling is historically linked to the prayer of Prophet Noah (peace be upon him) during the Flood, serving as a precedent for maintaining ritual purity and devotion amidst chaotic environmental conditions.
